lpplsF: Log-Periodic Power Law Singularity Model for Financial Bubbles

Source: R/lpplsF-package.R
lpplsF-package.Rd

Implementation of the LPPLS model for detecting and analysing financial bubbles, based on the calibration methods of Filimonov & Sornette (2013) and the Modified Profile Likelihood inference from Filimonov, Demos & Sornette (2017).

Fitting

fit_lppls

Calibrate the model to a log-price series

eval_lppls

Evaluate the model at given parameters

SSE

The objective the calibration minimises

Diagnosing a calibration

A calibration can look convincing as a plot and still not be worth interpreting: the estimate may rest on an optimisation bound, the per-tc searches may have settled in different local optima, and the modified profile likelihood may be undefined over part of the tc grid. Printing the object returned by fit_lppls reports on all of this, and the rest go further.

print

The estimate together with the checks that decide whether to trust it; warnings are listed only when something is wrong, so a clean calibration reports none

summary

The same diagnostics as values, plus the curvature check and whether each likelihood interval is closed by the likelihood or by the edge of the grid

plot

Any plot attached at fit time, or the basin views, which show whether the per-tc searches split into a good and an inferior cluster

lppls_curvature

Whether the estimate sits at a genuine interior minimum, which is what the modified profile likelihood assumes

residual_qq_plot

Calibration residuals against a normal or fitted Student-t reference

Rolling windows and Lagrange regularization

Each of these returns an object that summarises itself when printed.

lppls_rolling

Recalibrate over a rolling start time \(T_1\), holding the end of the window fixed

lppls_lagrange

Lagrange regularization of a rolling calibration, locating the onset \(T_1^*\)

lr_trend_test

Whether the fitted bias trend is distinguishable from noise, by parametric bootstrap

rolling_tc_plot

\(\hat{t}_c\) and its likelihood intervals against \(T_1\)

rolling_param_plot

Each estimated parameter against \(T_1\)

chi_sq_np_plot, chi_sq_lambda_plot

The Lagrange diagnostics \(\chi^2_{np}(T_1)\) and \(\chi^2_{\lambda}(T_1)\)

Visualising the model and its landscape

fit_plot

A calibrated series with its fitted LPPLS curve

sse_contour_plot

SSE over a grid of two parameters

sse_surface_plot

The same landscape as an interactive or a static surface

Model Description

The LPPLS model describes the log-price dynamics of financial assets approaching a critical point (bubble peak or crash):

$$y(t) = A + (t_c - t)^m [B + C_1 \cos(\omega \log(t_c - t)) + C_2 \sin(\omega \log(t_c - t))]$$

where:

  • \(t_c\) is the critical time

  • \(m\) is the power law exponent (typically 0.1-0.9)

  • \(\omega\) is the log-periodic frequency (typically 6-13)

  • \(A, B, C_1, C_2\) are linear parameters

Optimization Modes

F1

Simultaneous optimization of all nonlinear parameters

F2

Two-stage: optimize (m, omega) for each tc, then select best tc

MPL

Modified profile likelihood, with likelihood intervals for tc

References

Filimonov, V., & Sornette, D. (2013). A stable and robust calibration scheme of the log-periodic power law model. Physica A, 392(17), 3698-3707.

Filimonov, V., Demos, G., & Sornette, D. (2017). Modified profile likelihood inference and interval forecast of the burst of financial bubbles. Quantitative Finance, 17(8), 1167-1186.
